learning_outcomes.text: Understand the physical principles that determine the generation and transmission of environmental noise and apply them to predict noise distribution in different environments.
Measure, analyze, and evaluate environmental noise levels as well as the acoustic properties of sources, enclosures, barriers, walls, and other elements with implications for sound fields.
Design, calculate, and execute projects for acoustic insulation and conditioning of enclosures and noise sources.
Conduct acoustic environmental impact studies and design corrective actions for their control.
Handle mandatory legislation and regulations regarding environmental noise.

syllabus_topics: Generation and transmission. Basic sound fields
Noise from machinery and installations. Damping

assessment_methods.method: Theoretical and practical exam on the taught material
Classroom participation and deliverables from exercises, assignments, and presentations in classroom practices
Laboratory, field, and computer lab participation, reports, and exam

assessment_rules: To pass by continuous assessment, a minimum score of 4 out of 10 must be obtained in each section, and at least 5 out of 10 in the total weighted score. Students who do not meet these minimums may pass the course by passing a final written exam, which will cover all theoretical and practical content taught throughout the course, and will then have a weighting of 100% in the final grade. Extraordinary calls and differentiated assessments will follow this same single written exam modality, covering all theoretical and practical content with a 100% weighting in the final grade. Order, cleanliness, general presentation, appropriate writing, absence of spelling errors, clarity, logical structure, level of detail in problem solving, and use of appropriate units will be considered during grading. The use of incorrect units that do not maintain dimensional consistency will be considered particularly serious, as will invalid, outlandish, or physically impossible results.
